items.title: Body of Indian national found, seventh victim of Sungai Pertak water surge, one still missing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The body of the seventh victim of the water surge incident at the Sungai Pertak Picnic Site near here was found at 3.40pm today, leaving only one of the eight people reported missing still unaccounted for. According to the latest information from the Incident Command Post (PKTK), the body of the adult Indian national was found in Sector C of the search area. Today’s SAR operation began at 7am, with additional personnel from the Special Tactical Operations and Rescue Team Malaysia of the Fire and Rescue Department.

items.title: Najib spends nearly eight hours out of Taman Duta residence for Friday prayers, returns at 6.27pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak returned to his residence in Taman Duta at about 6.27pm today, concluding an outing that lasted nearly eight hours. The former leader was spotted leaving for Friday prayers this morning before making his way back to his residence in the evening. Najib is currently serving the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest at his Jalan Langgak Duta residence until August 23, 2028, following a conditional royal pardon granted in September.

items.title: Former MAG chief Izham Ismail appointed to Maybank board
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has appointed former Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) group managing director and airline group chief executive officer Datuk Captain Izham Ismail as an independent non-executive director effective Nov 15. Maybank announced the appointment in a Bursa Malaysia filing today. Izham, 65, led MAG as group managing director and airline group CEO from 2017 until 2026, retiring from the airline group on Jan 31 this year.

items.title: Selangor allocates RM559mil to replace ageing water pipes
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Selangor has allocated RM559 million in its 2027 Budget to replace ageing water pipes as part of efforts to improve the state's water supply system. Another RM143.2 million has been allocated to upgrade water treatment plants, while RM209.2 million will go towards the Water Grid Connectivity project. The project aims to achieve 100 per cent connectivity for 36 dam terminals by the end of 2028, strengthening the water supply systems in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya.

items.title: Amirudin unveils ‘Kita Selangor’ special financial aid with two months’ salary for civil servants, minimum RM1,000
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 13 — The Selangor State Government today announced a Special Financial Assistance (BKK) equivalent to two months’ salary for civil servants in the state. “The state government is announcing the ‘Kita Selangor’ Special Financial Assistance (BKK) for the year 2026, amounting to two months’ salary or allowance, with a minimum payment of RM1,000. Meanwhile, Amirudin said the state government proposed an increase in the monthly allowance for KAFA teachers by RM200, raising the total allowance from RM1,500 to RM1,700 starting from January 2027.

items.title: Selangor to give 5,000 p-hailing riders RM100 monthly voucher
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Some 5,000 registered p-hailing riders in Selangor will receive RM100 monthly, or RM1,200 annually, under the Kita Selangor Gig Voucher initiative announced in the Selangor 2027 Budget. Amirudin said the voucher would be complemented by technology exposure and industry training through short courses conducted by the Selangor Technical Skills Development Centre (STDC). The programme, including training, would receive an allocation of RM10 million, he said.

items.title: Amirudin: Sungai Klang, Sungai Langat among river basins in Selangor’s RM36.45m flood mitigation plan
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 13 — The Selangor government has allocated RM36.45 million for 47 immediate flood mitigation projects under the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (JPS) for 2027. He said the allocation would also cover the Sungai Buloh, Sungai Selangor, Sungai Bernam and Sungai Kapar Besar river basins, as well as preparatory works such as design, surveying and land matters. Amirudin also said that RM19.38 million had been allocated for 25 irrigation system projects, RM17.90 million for 16 river basin development and management projects, and RM6.63 million for nine environmentally friendly irrigation projects.

items.title: Seventh victim found after water surge at Sungai Pertak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The body of an Indian citizen was found during a search and rescue operation following a water surge at Sungai Luit, Kampung Orang Asli Pertak, Kuala Kubu Baru. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department director Datuk Wan Md Razali Wan Ismail said the seventh body was found at 3.40pm in Sector C of the search area. He said the body was taken to Sungai Buloh Hospital.

items.title: MB: Selangor budgets RM559m for 6,000km of ageing pipes, RM3.5m for water master plan
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 13 — The Selangor government has allocated RM559 million next year to replace ageing pipes in the state to ensure a more stable water supply for consumers. “However, starting from 2024, the state government and Air Selangor Sdn Bhd (Air Selangor) have increased the replacement rate to 300km annually,” he said when tabling the Selangor 2027 Budget here today. Meanwhile, Amirudin said the state government had also allocated RM120.8 million for the Non-Revenue Water (NRW) Reduction Programme, which includes the installation of Pressure Transient and Permanent Leak Noise Correlating Loggers (PLNCL) and Advanced Pressure Management Systems (APMS).

items.title: Selangor allocates RM24m to boost public transport use to 60pc, says MB
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 13 — The Selangor state government has allocated RM24 million for the public transport sector in 2027, aiming to increase public transport usage among state residents to 60 per cent from the current 40 per cent. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the allocation would support efforts to develop a more people-friendly public transport ecosystem, including improving bus services, providing fare subsidies and expanding pedestrian routes. “To develop a well-structured first- and last-mile connectivity system that complements a comprehensive public transport ecosystem in Selangor, the state government has allocated RM24 million for the sector in 2027,” he said when tabling the Selangor Budget 2027 at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly here today.

items.title: WCT Holdings appoints Lai Cheng Yee as group MD
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: WCT Holdings Bhd has appointed Lai Cheng Yee as its group managing director (MD) beginning today. "Lai joined WCT Holdings as director (executive chairman's office) on Aug 15, 2018, assisting the executive chairman across all the group's businesses. Lai holds 13,527 shares in WCT Holdings.

items.title: Federal Court sets Feb 25 to hear Altantuya family’s leave to appeal over reduced RM1.4m award
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 13 — The Federal Court has fixed February 25 next year to hear an application by the family of murdered Mongolian national Altantuya Shaariibuu for leave to appeal against a Court of Appeal ruling that reduced the damages awarded over her death in 2006. He said the court also set Dec 3 to hear the family’s application to amend its notice of motion seeking leave to appeal, following case management before Federal Court deputy registrar Rohaiza Hamzah yesterday. Altantuya’s family filed the leave application on February 19 this year after the Court of Appeal reduced the damages awarded to them from RM5 million to RM1.4 million.

items.title: Altantuya family's bid to appeal damages set for Feb 25
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Federal Court has fixed Feb 25 next year to hear an application by Altantuya Shaariibuu's family for leave to appeal against a ruling reducing damages over her murder. He said the court also fixed Dec 3 to hear the family's application to amend its notice of motion seeking leave to appeal. Altantuya's family filed the leave application on Feb 19 this year after the Court of Appeal reduced the damages awarded to them from RM5 million to RM1.4 million.

items.title: It’s final: Dutch model Ivana Smit’s mother stops pursuing lawsuit against govt over probe of 2017 death
items.summary: This brings Smit’s family’s six-year legal bid in court to an end, but Sankara said the authorities should continue to investigate her death and to regularly communicate with her family. “Ivana’s family has decided not to seek leave to appeal to the Federal Court against the Court of Appeal’s decision of October 14, 2026. The Court of Appeal decision was not in Smit’s family’s favour.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM NOV 13, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's key index ended the week lower, dragged down by external uncertainties on stretched valuations in AI-related stocks. The FBM KLCI dropped more than three points to close at 1,582. In the crypto market, Bitcoin tumbled to RM281,497.

items.title: Sabah east coast security boosts tourism confidence
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah's east coast has recorded no kidnapping cases since Jan 15, 2020, boosting foreign tourists' confidence in the area's security. Sabah Police Commissioner Datuk Victor Sanjos said the achievement was the result of continued efforts by previous leaders and close cooperation among various agencies to maintain security. "Improved security has allowed development along Sabah's east coast to progress and created more economic opportunities for local communities.

items.title: DXN eyes Venezuela opportunities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: DXN Holdings Bhd has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Venezuela's La Guaira Special Economic Zone (La Guaira SEZ) to explore potential investment and business opportunities in sustainable agriculture, aquaculture, agro-processing and manufacturing. The MoU was signed in Caracas by La Guaira SEZ sole auhority Marcos Meléndez and DXN project director Foo Wai Leong. The Venezuelan government established La Guaira SEZ in 2023 to attract domestic and foreign investment to La Guaira.

items.title: Melaka polls: Ab Rauf leads 3,000-strong motorcycle convoy in Tanjung Bidara
items.summary: MASJID TANAH: More than 3,000 motorcycles took part in a Barisan Nasional convoy across the Tanjung Bidara state constituency on the final day of campaigning for the Melaka election today. The convoy, held as part of a flash mob programme, was led by Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh, who is also the coalition's candidate for the Tanjung Bidara seat. Ab Rauf also urged voters to fulfil their responsibility by casting their ballots tomorrow.

items.title: Ringgit ends mostly higher against major currencies, eases versus greenback
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended mostly higher against major currencies but eased against the US dollar on Friday as the greenback continued its upward momentum on a hawkish US interest rate outlook. The market has been expecting a sizeable interest rate hike by the US Federal Reserve (Fed) when the American central bank meets in December. The ringgit traded mostly higher against a basket of major currencies.

items.title: Melaka polls: 240 polling centres to open tomorrow for 675,166 electors, says EC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — A total of 240 polling centres involving 1,213 streams across Melaka will open tomorrow for 675,166 registered electors to cast their ballots in the 16th Melaka State Election. Election Commission (EC) secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said 11,103 personnel have been assigned to ensure smooth voting at all the polling centres. He said the EC has also completed checking all voting equipment, including ballot boxes, election ink, ballot papers and voting booths, ensuring they are in good condition before distribution to Presiding Officers (KTM) at each stream.

items.title: Selangor announces two-month special financial aid for civil servants
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The Selangor government today announced a Special Financial Assistance (BKK) payment equivalent to two months' salary for state civil servants. "The state government is announcing the 'Kita Selangor' Special Financial Assistance (BKK) for the year 2026, amounting to two months' salary or allowance, with a minimum payment of RM1,000. "God willing, the 'Kita Selangor' BKK will be disbursed by Dec 21," he said while tabling the Selangor 2027 Budget today.

items.title: AAPA adopts four aviation resolutions, urges government support amid rising fuel costs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Association of Asia Pacific Airlines (AAPA) has adopted four resolutions covering aviation sustainability, passenger rights, cabin safety and aviation security, while calling on governments to support airlines facing sharply higher fuel prices and operating costs. AAPA director general Wong Hong said Asia Pacific airlines are operating in a more challenging environment compared with 12 months ago. AAPA also called for closer cooperation among governments, aviation regulators and industry stakeholders to address common challenges and strengthen the long-term competitiveness of Asia Pacific aviation.

items.title: Melaka polls: Morning cloudy weather; some afternoon thunderstorms, says MetMalaysia
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 13 — The 16th Melaka State Election will be held tomorrow, and the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) forecasts that all three districts in the state, namely Melaka Tengah, Jasin and Alor Gajah, will experience cloudy weather in the morning. MetMalaysia, through its official portal, also forecasts that several places in these three districts will experience thunderstorms in the afternoon. For the latest news on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026 — Bernama

items.title: Lawyer: Former model's family will not appeal RM1.1mil damages ruling
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The family of Dutch model Ivana Smit will not appeal a ruling overturning a RM1.1 million damages award over alleged police negligence in the investigation into her death. The family's lawyer, Datuk Sankara Nair, said it would not seek leave to appeal to the Federal Court against the Court of Appeal's decision in October, bringing the civil proceedings to an end. In October, the Court of Appeal set aside a High Court ruling ordering the government to pay RM1.1 million in damages to the mother of Dutch model Ivana Smit over alleged negligence in the investigation into her daughter's death.

items.title: Policeman injured in parang attack can now move fingers after surgery
items.summary: Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad had informed the cabinet of the update during its meeting today. He said the Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had also expressed concern over the attack. Yesterday, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the complex replantation surgery took eight hours and was performed by HKL's Upper Limb and Microsurgery subspecialty team, led by Dr Allan Ravi Rajagopal and Dr Aziz Sabbir Husain.

items.title: UEC holders: No change to entry requirements for private medical degrees, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The government has agreed today to maintain the existing minimum entry requirements for Unified Examination Certificate (UEC) holders seeking admission into medical programmes at private higher education institutions. Fahmi, who is also the unity government spokesman, said UEC holders who meet the minimum requirement of a ‘B4’ grade in five specified subjects remain eligible to apply for admission into medical degree programmes at private higher education institutions. “The Cabinet agreed to maintain the minimum entry requirements for UEC holders intending to pursue medical programmes,” he said during a post-Cabinet media conference that was broadcast live today.

items.title: Najib performs Friday prayers in Kajang Prison
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak performed Friday prayers in Kajang Prison today, the Prisons Department confirmed. This was Najib's first Friday prayers since being allowed to spend the remainder of his SRC International jail sentence under house arrest at his residence in Jalan Langgak Duta, Taman Duta. Yesterday, his son, Datuk Mohd Nazifuddin, had said Najib would perform Friday prayers in Kajang Prison, in line with stipulations from the Prisons Department.

items.title: Kedah MB's daughter injured in motorcycle crash
items.summary: ALOR STAR: Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor's daughter was seriously injured when her motorcycle crashed near Kampung Alor Setol. Sanusi said his third child remained in the ICU for close monitoring and further tests to check for possible internal injuries. Meanwhile, Kota Setar district police chief Assistant Commissioner Syed Basri Syed Ali said preliminary investigations found that the accident occurred about 4pm when the 20-year-old was riding a Yamaha X-Max 250 from her college in Pokok Sena towards Alor Star.

items.title: Melaka polls: Stop all campaigning by 11.59pm tonight, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 13 — All candidates contesting the 16th Melaka State Election have been reminded to cease all campaign activities, including on social media platforms, by 11.59pm tonight, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said the Election Commission (EC) reminder must be complied with, meaning no new posts or content that could be construed as campaigning should appear on candidates’ social media accounts from midnight tonight through tomorrow. “So, no new posts on social media nearing midnight tonight.

items.title: Cabinet seeks AG’s advice on proposal to declassify Najib’s pardon board minutes, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The process of declassifying documents from the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting concerning former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak is underway and being carried out in accordance with existing laws, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. “It (the matter) was not explicitly raised during today’s Cabinet meeting, but I understand that the process is underway. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail was reported as saying in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday that he would put forward the proposal to declassify Najib’s Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting minutes to the Cabinet for consideration.

items.title: 1,764 flood victims remain at 12 relief centres in three states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 1,764 flood victims from 475 families remain housed at 12 temporary relief centres across three states as at 4.30pm today. In Perak, 274 victims from 79 families are housed at two relief centres in the Hilir Perak district. In Sarawak, 35 victims from six families remain at two relief centres across the Kuching and Miri districts.

items.title: Anwar concerned over safety protocols for police following Kepong attack, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has expressed concern over the safety of police officers following an incident in Kepong two days ago in which a police officer was attacked and had his right hand severed. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said existing procedures allow police officers to take necessary action to protect themselves. He added that Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail had also clarified that current protocols allow police officers to prioritise their own safety.

items.title: Two Bangladeshis nabbed as Penang Immigration officers bust fake e-pass syndicate
items.summary: SEBERANG JAYA: The Penang Immigration Department crippled a fake immigration e-pass printing syndicate and arrested two Bangladeshi men in Simpang Ampat last night. State Immigration director Syamsul Fitry Ahmad said the suspects, aged 23 and 32, were detained during a 10pm raid at a rented house following public tip-offs and days of intelligence gathering. Syamsul Fitry said further checks revealed the forged documents were linked to the construction sector, with the syndicate targeting undocumented or overstaying Bangladeshi and Pakistani nationals.

items.title: PAS accuses Malaysiakini of taking Hadi’s remarks out of context, rejects racial narrative
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — PAS has accused Malaysiakini of publishing a misleading report on its president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang’s remarks, claiming they were taken out of context. In a statement posted on Hadi’s Facebook page today, the PAS president’s office expressed regret over the report titled “ Sejahat-jahat orang Islam tak sezalim bukan Islam ” (Even the worst Muslim is not as cruel as a non-Muslim), saying it misrepresented the context of Hadi’s speech. “We regret the media narrative, which could cause misunderstandings among the public, and reject any attempt to stir up racial sentiments ahead of polling day for the Melaka state election,” the statement said.

items.title: Melaka election: Parties told to stop campaigning by midnight
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Political parties, candidates and their supporters must stop all campaigning, including on social media, by 11.59pm tonight ahead of Saturday's Melaka election. Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said parties should not publish new campaign-related content after the deadline set by the Election Commission (EC). He said candidates and parties should issue their final campaign messages early to avoid breaching election rules.

items.title: Prisons Department aims to expand family rehab programme nationwide to curb recidivism
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL: The Prisons Department plans to expand a new family and parenting rehabilitation module nationwide to reduce recidivism rates among inmates. Prisons Deputy Commissioner-General (Security and Correctional) Rosoman Abu Bakar @ Che Din said the pioneer initiative, Kompas Sejahtera, equipped inmates with essential life skills prior to their reintegration into society. He said the pilot run involved 30 facilitators from the northern zone correctional institutions — covering Penang, Kedah, Perlis and Perak — and directly benefited 224 male inmates at the Seberang Prai Prison.

items.title: Bursa courts regional retail investors via new partnership
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia Bhd is seeking to widen foreign retail participation in the local stock market through a partnership with Singapore brokerage Phillip Nova, as it looks to attract more regional investors to Malaysian-listed companies. The collaboration, launched in Singapore on Nov 7 under Bursa Malaysia's Invest Beyond Borders initiative, is intended to give Singapore-based retail investors easier access to Malaysian equities through Phillip Nova's digital trading platform. The companies were Top Glove Corp Bhd, Karex Bhd, Inta Bina Group Bhd, Sunway Healthcare Holdings Bhd, Hi-Mobility Bhd and Kee Ming Group Bhd.

items.title: Former Perlis MB Azlan Man faces Jan 20, 2027 decision in RM1.18m false claims trial
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The Sessions Court here will decide on Jan 20 whether former Perlis Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Azlan Man will be called to enter his defence or acquitted of 10 charges involving alleged false claims and receiving proceeds of illegal activities. Earlier, Deputy Public Prosecutor Noralis Mat submitted that Azlan had made five claims for overseas travel facilities between 2013 and 2017, purportedly in his capacity as Menteri Besar, although investigations found that the trips did not take place on the stated dates. Noralis said the testimony of the 17th prosecution witness, former Assistant Accountant at the Management Services Division of the Perlis State Secretary’s Office, Mohd Aswad Abdul Razak, established that claims for overseas holiday travel facilities could not be converted into cash.

items.title: Malaysia-Indonesia ties remain strong despite Gibran's resignation, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia-Indonesia ties will remain unaffected by the resignation of Indonesian vice-president Gibran Rakabuming Raka, said government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said the political developments in Indonesia would not affect the longstanding ties between the neighbouring countries. "Relations between the two countries will remain intact and remain good.

items.title: One-handed mechanic repairs up to five motorcycles a day
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Despite losing an arm in a 2019 motorcycle crash, a 32-year-old mechanic here can still repair up to five motorcycles a day using only one hand. Samsul Aripin Sadip, from Kota Tinggi, said many people are amazed by his ability to fix motorcycles with one hand and often assume he was born that way. Although they were initially distressed by what happened, I rested for a few months before retraining myself to repair motorcycles using my left hand.

items.title: Anwar raps agencies over repeated flooding in Selangor, orders immediate action
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today criticised government agencies for failing to address flooding in Selangor, calling it unacceptable that residents are forced to endure flooding four to five times a year. Speaking to reporters after performing Friday prayers in Brickfields here, Anwar said repeated disruptions continue to place a heavy burden on the public, even if floodwaters do not reach high levels. “Following my engagement with Cabinet ministers and the Selangor state government yesterday, I convened a meeting in Parliament to address the ongoing flood crisis,” he said.

items.title: Najib pardon minutes set for declassification process
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The process of declassifying minutes of the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting concerning former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's conditional pardon is being arranged, subject to legal requirements. Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the process was under way. Yesterday, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail told Parliament that he would propose at today's cabinet meeting that the minutes of the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting concerning Najib's conditional pardon be declassified.

items.title: Anwar praises HKL surgeons' feat in reattaching cop's hand
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) surgeons for reattaching a policeman's severed hand following a parang attack in Kepong. Anwar said he had told the cabinet meeting earlier that the government must support the security forces. Following the successful surgery, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry remained committed to ensuring Thierry received comprehensive medical care to support his recovery and restore optimal hand function.

items.title: Selangor told to speed up drain, river cleaning to reduce floods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Selangor needs to speed up drain and river cleaning to reduce flooding, following Kuala Lumpur's example, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. "The menteri besar (Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari) has approved additional funding and action at all levels. "In Kuala Lumpur, drains and rivers are cleaned six times a year instead of twice, helping to reduce flooding," he said.

items.title: 64,100 litres of diesel worth RM1.07mil seized in Kedah raid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Authorities seized 64,100 litres of suspected misappropriated diesel worth RM439,085 and arrested four people, including a foreigner, during a raid at an industrial premises in Kedah on Wednesday. "The seizures involved two tanker lorries containing about 4,500 litres and 14,000 litres of diesel respectively, as well as three skid tanks containing about 18,000 litres, 13,000 litres and 14,000 litres of the fuel. "Also seized were an intermediate bulk container (IBC) tank holding about 600 litres of diesel, two oil suction pumps, two metered suction pumps, three mobile phones, as well as equipment and vehicle keys believed to be linked to the activity," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Anwar plays down Cabinet tensions, says ‘no need to rush’ on Loke’s resignation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today described the mood at this morning’s Cabinet meeting as “normal”, amid signs of disunity within the government as his Pakatan Harapan coalition goes head-to-head with its unity government ally, Barisan Nasional, in tomorrow’s Melaka state polls. Anwar played down the tension in the run-up to tomorrow’s vote as part and parcel of an election campaign, and said he anticipates the temperature to cool down again once the election is done. Media reports suggested there is growing friction within Anwar’s Cabinet, as the two major governing coalitions traded salvos at the Melaka election campaign trail where incumbent BN had teamed up with rivals Perikatan Nasional to defend the state.

items.title: UEC holders remain eligible to take up medical degrees at private universities
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Unified Examination Certificate (UEC) holders who meet the minimum entry requirement of B4 in five stipulated subjects will remain eligible to apply for direct entry into medical degree programmes at private universities. "Therefore, UEC holders who meet the minimum requirement of B4 in the five stipulated subjects remain eligible to apply for direct entry into medical degree programmes at private higher education institutions (IPTS)," he said at his weekly post-cabinet meeting press conference. Under existing MMC guidelines, UEC qualifications are recognised for admission into medical programmes at private higher education institutions only.

items.title: N. Sembilan police begin deployment of 261 personnel for Melaka election
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 13 — A total of 261 police officers and personnel from Negeri Sembilan have been deployed to help ensure smooth and orderly polling in the 16th Melaka State Election tomorrow. Negeri Sembilan Police Chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the deployment began yesterday to facilitate early preparations for polling. — Bernama

items.title: Melaka polls: Rafie vows inclusive development for Paya Rumput residents
items.summary: MELAKA: Perikatan Nasional candidate for Paya Rumput Rafie Ahmad wants to continue the development initiatives undertaken by the previous assemblyman while addressing residents' concerns over flooding and traffic congestion in the constituency. He said he also wanted to address the needs of residents as Paya Rumput continued to experience population growth. "My hopes for Paya Rumput go beyond seeing taller buildings or wider roads.

items.title: High Court dismisses application to remove administrators of Genting heiress’ RM1.6b estate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The High Court here today dismissed an application by the son of the late Genting heiress Lim Siew Kim to remove two interim administrators overseeing the RM1.6 billion estate. Judge Datuk Mahazan Mat Taib dismissed Marcus Chan Jau Chwen’s application against lawyer Datuk S. Satharuban and Khoo Siew Kiat and ordered him to pay RM30,000 in costs to the two administrators. The court also discharged the interim injunction restraining the two from acting as administrators of the estate, allowing them to resume their duties under the court’s supervision.

items.title: ‘The next move is yours’: Umno tells DAP to talk, not threaten, amid Najib pardon row
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Umno has urged DAP to resolve its differences with coalition partners through dialogue and consultation, instead of issuing public ultimatums or demanding resignations, following the controversy over Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s conditional pardon. Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said, described DAP chairman Gobind Singh Deo’s call for Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi to resign if he did not support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s leadership, as regrettable and unhelpful to the unity government’s stability. Azalina, who is also Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform), said the agreement did not require coalition partners to agree unconditionally with every political position taken by the prime minister or other political leaders.

items.title: Cops await DPP instructions for 15 more cases of impersonating Selangor Raja Muda’s aide-de-camp
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 13 — The police are awaiting instructions from the office of the Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) regarding 15 more cases of individuals impersonating the aide-de-camp (ADC) of the Raja Muda of Selangor in vehicle and property transactions. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said that 17 investigation papers have been opened based on the police reports received, and all of them have been completed before being referred to the Selangor DPP office for further instructions. “As for the other 15 cases, the police are waiting for feedback from the DPP’s office for any further instructions,” he said at the Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) media conference at the Selangor police contingent headquarters (IPK) here today.

items.title: Rosmah’s defamation suit: Nov 24 hearing for Harith Iskander’s lawyers to discharge themselves
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The High Court here today fixed November 24 to hear an application by lawyers Sangeet Kaur Deo and Harkiranjit Kaur Manjit Singh to discharge themselves from representing comedian and actor Harith Iskander in a defamation suit filed by Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor. “Yes, we have applied to discharge ourselves from representing (Harith Iskander),” Sangeet confirmed when contacted. The case management proceedings for the application were held online today before Judge Arziah Mohamed Apandi, with Sangeet and Harkiranjit attending alongside Rosmah’s lawyers, Mohamed Baharudeen Mohamed Ariff and Nur-Diana Ezlyn Hashim.

items.title: IRB’s RM1.69b appeal in Najib bankruptcy case set for Feb 23; no appeal for Nazifuddin
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 13 — The Federal Court has fixed February 23 next year to hear the Inland Revenue Board’s (IRB) application for leave to appeal against the Court of Appeal’s decision granting former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak a stay of bankruptcy proceedings against him. Wee also confirmed that the IRB had not filed an application for leave to appeal against the Court of Appeal’s decision granting a stay of bankruptcy proceedings against Najib’s son, Datuk Mohd Nazifuddin. On September 4, the Court of Appeal ruled in favour of Najib and Mohd Nazifuddin, allowing their applications to stay the bankruptcy proceedings pending the disposal of their appeals before the Special Commissioners of Income Tax (SCIT) over additional tax assessments issued by the IRB.

items.title: ‘Corruption is corruption’: Saifuddin takes aim at Hadi over remarks on Muslim, non-Muslim leaders
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Nov 13 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail has criticised PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang over his remarks that even the worst Muslim government is less oppressive than a non-Muslim administration, saying leaders should be judged by their integrity and actions, not religion. In a statement today, Saifuddin Nasution said such comparisons were regrettable as they risked using religion to divide society and excuse wrongdoing by political leaders. He said Islam taught Muslims to uphold justice even towards those they disliked, citing verse eight of Surah Al-Maidah, which states: “Do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just.

items.title: Survey: BN-Perikatan poised to dominate in Melaka as Pakatan-Bersatu grassroots synergy sputters
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Backchannel political cooperation has not generated grassroots synergy for Pakatan Harapan (PH) and Bersatu in the Melaka state election, leaving an openly coordinated Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional (BN-PN) pact on course to claim up to 24 seats, according to think tank Ilham Centre. According to Ilham’s findings, 91 per cent of PN supporters expressed readiness to vote for BN candidates, while 78 per cent of BN voters were willing to back PN contenders. Under their shared electoral slate, BN is contesting 23 of Melaka’s 28 seats, with PN fielding candidates in the remaining five.

items.title: Zero cases of overpricing under Deepavali 2026 festive price control scheme, Domestic Trade Ministry reports
items.summary: KPDN Enforcement director-general Datuk Azman Adam said the achievement reflected an improvement in trader compliance compared with last year, when six violations involving the sale of goods above the controlled prices were recorded. He said that, overall, the number of enforcement cases taken by the KPDN during the implementation of the Deepavali 2026 SHMMP increased to 482, compared with 445 last year. “Of the total, 481 cases involved the retail sector and one the wholesale sector, compared with 444 retail cases and one wholesale case last year,” he added.

items.title: Hadi urges Melaka Muslims to vote, warns non-Muslims could take power if they stay home
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 13 — With Melaka voters heading to the polls tomorrow, PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang has urged Muslims to turn out and vote, warning that staying away could allow non-Muslims to take power. Among those who addressed the crowd were Pejuang president Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir, MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong, Wawasan president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin and Gerakan president Datuk Dominic Lau. Also present were Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan, PAS deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man and Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.

items.title: Police foil attempt to smuggle over 9kg of syabu worth RM476,180 to Indonesia via Port Dickson jetty
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 13 — Negeri Sembilan police foiled an attempt to smuggle 9.238 kilogrammes (kg) of drugs believed to be syabu (methamphetamine), worth RM476,180, to Indonesia at the Port Dickson Passenger Jetty Terminal here two days ago. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said an Indonesian man, in his 20s and believed to be a drug mule, was also arrested after he was spotted acting suspiciously while carrying a medium-sized black suitcase at the terminal at about 9.30am. He said that upon inspecting the suitcase, police found a modified compartment used to conceal six packages containing about five kg of drugs believed to be syabu, along with clothing.

items.title: No indication AI chips were exported from Malaysia in Nvidia-Megaspeed case, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — There has been no indication that artificial intelligence chips linked to the Nvidia-Megaspeed issue were exported from Malaysia, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar also said the Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti) had given a report on the matter this morning. To a question on whether Malaysia had received a formal request from Singapore or the United States regarding any probe on the Nvidia-Megaspeed issue, Anwar said Malaysia has not received any formal request from Singapore or the United States regarding the issue.
